In its 3Q 2025 earnings transcript (period ended September 30, 2025, published October 16, 2025), Schwab says that in its advisor services business it is deepening relationships with the 16,000 RIA firms it serves by building a broader support ecosystem beyond custody, and has grown its lending support, alternatives capability, and institutional no-transaction-fee mutual fund platform: "In our advisor services business, we're deepening relationships with the 16,000 RIA firms we serve by building a broader support ecosystem that extends beyond custody alone to add value for RIAs. We've grown our lending support, alternatives capability, and expanded our institutional no-transaction fee mutual fund platform."

In its 2025 10-K (period ended December 31, 2025, published February 25, 2026), Schwab says that in addition to focusing on superior service, it uses technology to provide RIAs with a highly developed, scalable platform for administering their clients' assets easily and efficiently.

Trade press (published October 29, 2026) reports that Wurster cited the growing use of pledged-asset lending balances, the demand for long-short investment strategies, and the need to make private-market investing more accessible to the masses as focus areas for Schwab's custody offerings: "Wurster cited the growing use of pledged-asset lending balances, the demand for long-short investment strategies, and the need to make private-market investing more accessible to the masses as focus areas for its custody offerings."

In its 4Q 2024 earnings transcript (period ended December 31, 2024, published January 21, 2025), Schwab says that in advisor services it is adding support and capabilities for RIAs of all sizes while also helping new advisors transition to independence: "In advisor services, we are adding support and capabilities for RIAs of all sizes while also helping new advisors transition to independence."

In its 2025 10-K (period ended December 31, 2025, published February 25, 2026), Schwab states that in the Advisor Services arena it competes with institutional custodians, wirehouses, regional and independent broker-dealers, fintech custodians, banks, and trust companies: "In the Advisor Services arena, we compete with institutional custodians, wirehouses, regional and independent broker-dealers, fintech custodians, banks, and trust companies."
Trade press (published October 29, 2026) reports that CEO Rick Wurster said independent advisors are competing against wirehouses that typically have strong banks attached to their advice.

In its 4Q 2025 earnings transcript (period ended December 31, 2025, published January 21, 2026), CEO Rick Wurster said RIAs compete from time to time against the wealth divisions of wirehouses: "They do, from time to time, compete against the wealth divisions of wirehouses."

In its 3Q 2026 earnings transcript (period ended September 30, 2026, published October 15, 2026), CEO Rick Wurster said Schwab changed the minimums for long/short strategies and throttled growth to some extent, while noting that advisor services NNA growth has not slowed: "as we look to October, where we have changed the minimums for long/short and throttled growth to some extent, the growth has in no way slowed at all in terms of AS NNA."

Trade press (published October 28, 2026) reports that Wurster said Schwab limited long-short offerings to clients with at least $10 million in assets, curtailing their use by many advisors: "That led the firm to limit long-short offerings only to clients with at least $10 million in assets , curtailing their use by many advisors."

Trade press (published October 28, 2026) reports that Wurster said Schwab reduced the Schwab Advisor Network referral network by raising the bar for participation to only clients with over $5 million and RIAs with at least $500 million in AUM: "reducing the Schwab Advisor Network referral network by raising the bar for participation to only clients with over $5 million and RIAs with at least $500 million in AUM ."

In its 2025 10-K (period ended December 31, 2025, published February 25, 2026), Schwab says that during the Ameritrade integration it experienced some expected attrition of client assets from retail accounts and RIAs, though such attrition was below its initial estimates: "we experienced some expected attrition of client assets from retail accounts and RIAs, though such attrition was below our initial estimates."
